problem: ISP routing/peering problem - sudden high ping or packet loss to Riot servers (fixed by Cloudflare WARP)
symptoms: Ping suddenly jumps (e.g. 12ms -> 80-180ms) or sticks at a fixed value only in Valorant while other games are fine
1-13% packet loss on wired connection starting for many users the same day
Region/ISP clusters: AT&T Fiber (Florida, Bay Area), Vocus-based ISPs in Australia (Brisbane/Perth/Sydney), MEO in Portugal
root_causes: ISP routing/peering to Riot servers degraded (not the player's PC); Riot/ISP must fix it

fixes.fix: Install and enable Cloudflare WARP (1.1.1.1 app, WARP mode) while playing; several OPs confirmed it restored normal ping/removed packet loss. Described as temporary until ISP/Riot fixes routing; ping may rise a few ms (5 -> 10).
Use another VPN (Urban VPN, PIA to Sydney, Mudfish) to bypass bad route
Flush DNS, quit Vanguard from tray, restart PC (one user said it helped for Portugal MEO case; others said it did not)
Contact ISP / Riot support about routing; nothing local to fix (MEO Portugal thread: users report waiting, later 'arranjaram')

diagnostic_signals: Traceroute/pathping to Riot server IPs and compare hop latency
Ping/packet loss to Riot servers over time (ping stuck at constant value)
Detect ISP name via public IP lookup (Vocus, AT&T, MEO) for known routing incidents
Compare ping with and without WARP/VPN

problem: VAN 185 disconnect ~15 min into match (ISP issue, VPN workaround) and console error 51
symptoms: Game crashes about 15 minutes after start with VAN 185
On console error 51/54 then VAN 185 after maintenance

fixes.fix: Use a free VPN (Cloudflare WARP, or Urban VPN connected to own country) to bypass ISP issue
Console: delete and reinstall the game (fixed error 51 for several users, may recur)

problem: VAN 293 - Vanguard error mid-match (every 30-60 min)
symptoms: VAN 293 after 10-60 minutes in game; after crash game won't relaunch until PC reboot
root_causes: Network-filtering/VPN software conflicting (VPN, Docker Desktop, NetLimiter)
Riot-side issue acknowledged by support for some users

fixes.fix: Open services.msc, set vgc service Startup type to Manual, start it, then launch the game (a poster says it worked)
Uninstall VPN software and Docker Desktop; the OP said deleting VPN fixed theirs
Disable NetLimiter (user confirmed it was the cause)
Enable Cloudflare WARP / 1.1.1.1

diagnostic_signals: Installed VPN, virtual adapters, Docker Desktop, NetLimiter running

problem: Valorant stuck at 20% / won't start due to VPN or virtual network adapters
symptoms: Game starts, progress bar reaches ~20% and nothing happens
root_causes: Leftover VPN (installed for Minecraft) / virtual adapters interfering

fixes.fix: Open Device Manager > Network adapters and disable virtual/unused adapters (VirtualBox, VMware, TAP-Windows, WAN); OP found a VPN installed by their son and removing it made it work

diagnostic_signals: Enumerate virtual/VPN network adapters (TAP, VMware, VirtualBox)

problem: VAN 57 / VAN 81 - Vanguard driver (vgk) not loading, needs a real boot cycle
symptoms: VAN 81 on Valorant / VAN 57 on League after weeks of reinstalls
Riot Client says OK to play after Vanguard reinstall but loops reinstall
root_causes: Vanguard driver needs an actual reboot to load; Riot Client restart check does not always detect it; stale C:\Windows\vgkbootstatus.dat

fixes.fix: Close all Riot processes; ipconfig /flushdns, /release, /renew; delete C:\Windows\vgkbootstatus.dat; uninstall Vanguard and reboot; let Riot Client reinstall Vanguard then REBOOT before pressing Play (do not press Play when client says ready)

problem: Vanguard never installs / installation loop / vgk.sys or vgc missing (VAN 83)
symptoms: Riot Client says 'Installing Vanguard' then silently fails; Play errors since Vanguard absent
C:\Program Files\Riot Vanguard folder empty or absent; vgc service does not exist (sc query vgc)
Installer files appear in temp then get deleted; vgc log filled with hex
root_causes: Installer files deleted/blocked from temp so Vanguard files and services are never created
Unknown (possible hardware/disk issue after BSOD during install - unresolved)

fixes.fix: Manual install: copy the temporary Vanguard folder from %TEMP% before it is deleted into C:\Program Files\Riot Vanguard\, then in admin cmd register the service: sc create vgc binPath= "C:\Program Files\Riot Vanguard\vgc.exe" type= own start= demand error= normal obj= LocalSystem (command truncated in data; verify) and start it; multiple users confirmed it worked
Make the user Temp folder undeletable during install (Deny Delete ACL via PowerShell Set-Acl, revert after) so files can be copied; a commenter confirmed success

Manual VGK/VGC install guide: recreate registry keys HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\vgc and \vgk from a working PC export (.reg) plus driver files; verify driver loaded with Sysinternals WinObj (not for ARM CPUs)
Case with BSOD mid-reinstall: reinstalling client/game, repair, cleanup did not help; ticket opened - no fix found

diagnostic_signals: Existence of C:\Program Files\Riot Vanguard folder and vgc.exe/vgk.sys
sc query vgc / vgk service existence

problem: Valorant failed to launch / 'Something unusual happened' after VAN 84
symptoms: 'Valorant failed to launch - something unusual happened', previously VAN84 fixed by force-restarting vgk/vgm
DevOverrideEnable registry suggestion did not help

fixes.fix: Completely uninstall Vanguard and Riot Client, manually delete leftover folders, reinstall Riot Client; first launch gives 'couldn't launch properly' error - fully close and reopen Riot Client, then launch again and it works
Another user tried that 15 times without success (AtlasOS Windows)

problem: Vanguard not initialized / reboot ends in automatic repair loop
symptoms: VANGUARD NOT INITIALIZED; restart leads to 'preparing automatic repair' and black screen
root_causes: Possibly leftover Vanguard files or unstable system/disk

fixes.fix: Fully uninstall game and anti-cheat with Revo Uninstaller or BCUninstaller, clean install both

diagnostic_signals: Disk/file system health, boot repair events

problem: Vanguard blocks chkdsk / file system repair at boot (dirty NTFS flag)
symptoms: Windows tries to repair file system every boot and fails; chkdsk /r gives access denied; volume dirty, TRIM disabled
root_causes: Vanguard driver loads at boot and prevents chkdsk from locking C: (poster's claim; commenters suspect failing SSD)

fixes.fix: Exit Vanguard from tray, or uninstall Vanguard and reboot so Windows can repair; run chkdsk C: /f /r manually then; Riot reinstalls Vanguard later. Alternatively boot Safe Mode. Run TRIM afterwards

diagnostic_signals: Volume dirty bit (fsutil dirty query C:)
chkdsk scheduled at boot / event log Chkdsk

problem: Riot Client/Valorant update stuck, endless 'Updating', file access error
symptoms: Update stuck for hours, 'Updating' with no progress bar
'Something unusual has happened while trying to access a file needed for the update'

fixes.fix: Close Riot processes in Task Manager; delete %localappdata%\Riot Games\Riot Client folder (only that folder; deletes login data/cache), restart; OP and several users confirmed; signing out and back in also worked for one
Delete the Riot Client folder in the Riot Games root while keeping Valorant/LoL folders, reinstall client, then Repair

diagnostic_signals: Riot Client process hung/updating; %localappdata%\Riot Games\Riot Client cache size

problem: Game crashes when opening Graphics Quality setting
symptoms: Crash (or 3-4 sec freeze) as soon as Graphics Quality is selected in Video settings
Repair/driver update/Vanguard reinstall did not help; other account works
root_causes: Corrupt per-account config (GameUserSettings) or bad install path (game on X: drive reported by support)

fixes.fix: Delete the config folder under %localappdata%\VALORANT\Saved (resets graphics/fps settings); confirmed by two OPs
Riot support clean reinstall: delete Riot Client folder in C:\Riot Games, delete %localappdata%\Riot Games, uninstall and reinstall (game was installed on a non-C drive); OP confirmed it worked

diagnostic_signals: Install path of Riot Client (non-C drive)

problem: Microstutter on alt-tab / Graphics Quality after Windows update or fresh Windows install
symptoms: Brief micro-freeze on alt-tab and Esc > Graphics Quality; FPS graphs smooth but feels like 30 fps
root_causes: Windows update KB5101650 (14 July 2026) blamed by users

fixes.fix: Uninstall Windows update KB5101650 (Settings > Windows Update > Update history > Uninstall updates); users report microstutter removed
Disable MPO via NVIDIA registry script (contested by others)

problem: FPS drop/lag after patch 13.01 (July 2026)
symptoms: FPS falls to 10-60 or feels laggy after update; some say actual fps unchanged but feels like 30
root_causes: Patch/new Vanguard build raising CPU use

fixes.fix: Redownload/reinstall Valorant and Vanguard (Revo Uninstaller full wipe); OPs confirmed fps recovered
Memory leak found with RAMMap (non-paged pool 90-95%) - clean Windows install fixed it
Restrict vgc.exe to a single CPU core via affinity (reported to fix 40% CPU usage)
Clean shader cache (Disk Cleanup > DirectX Shader Cache)
Turn off Nvidia/Adrenalin overlay

problem: Microstutter / periodic freezes caused by Realtek 2.5GbE or onboard LAN controller conflict with Vanguard
symptoms: Micro-stutter every few seconds even at high fps, vgc.exe CPU spikes, flat in-game fps graphs
Common on new AMD builds (9060XT, 9800X3D, 7800X3D, B650/B850/X870)
Event Viewer System log repeated Realtek PCIe 2.5GbE errors (rt25cx21 hardware I/O error, device unresponsive and reset)
root_causes: Realtek 2.5GbE driver/hardware I/O error colliding with Vanguard
Unused onboard LAN controller while on Wi-Fi

fixes.fix: Device Manager > Network adapters > disable the Realtek PCIe 2.5GbE controller (or unused onboard LAN) when using Wi-Fi; multiple OPs confirmed immediate fix. If using Ethernet, disable the wireless adapter instead or update/repair NIC driver
Check Event Viewer > System for repeated Realtek I/O errors to confirm
Also disable HAGS and set BIOS C-states from Auto to Enabled (one OP combo fix)
Reset BIOS to defaults except Secure Boot and EXPO fixed one user's stutter
Windows reinstall fixed one laptop case

diagnostic_signals: Event log System: Realtek / rt25cx21 / device reset warnings
Network adapters list (Realtek 2.5GbE enabled but unused)

problem: Valorant crash/freeze or system hang related to AMD iGPU (Ryzen desktop)
symptoms: Freeze then crash after mouse click in game; Event ID 1000 Vanguard errors; same in CS/OW
Entire PC hard-freezes ~100 seconds after launching Valorant (Kernel-Power 41), no BSOD
root_causes: Missing iGPU driver leaving an unknown display device (yellow warning in Device Manager) that Vanguard enumerates at startup

fixes.fix: Disable iGPU in BIOS (confirmed by OP, RX 7900XT + 7950X3D)
Install the missing AMD iGPU/chipset drivers so no device shows a yellow warning in Device Manager (confirmed by OP and another user; works with iGPU on or off)

diagnostic_signals: Device Manager devices with problem code / unknown display adapter
iGPU enabled in BIOS with no driver

problem: Kernel-Power 41 / whole-PC freeze or shutdown while playing Valorant
symptoms: Screen freezes, PC resets, Event Viewer Kernel-Power 41; CPU 100% before freeze
Laptop shuts down mid-game, Hyper-V-Hypervisor 'VMX not present or not enabled'
PC hard-freezes needing power button
root_causes: GPU driver version problems (RX cards) per one user

fixes.fix: Follow answeroverflow guide linked by OP (content not in thread); OP says Valorant ran fine afterwards (not confirmed permanent)
Roll back GPU driver to an older version (RX card issue)
sfc /scannow, DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth, bcdedit /set hypervisorlaunchtype auto; enable virtualization (helped for a few games only)

problem: Dell/Alienware STATUS_VMD_9001 - Intel VMD / RST conflict crash
symptoms: Instant crash at launch (or fatal VMD controller error within a minute of match) on Dell Slim ECS1250 / Alienware
root_causes: Intel Rapid Storage Technology VMD controller conflict with Vanguard (confirmed by Riot support)

fixes.fix: Disable VMD in BIOS safely: admin cmd 'bcdedit /set {current} safeboot minimal', reboot (boots Safe Mode), enter BIOS (F2/F12) and turn off VMD, then remove safeboot flag to return to normal boot; avoids BSOD (steps partly truncated in data); at least two users confirmed it works

diagnostic_signals: Intel VMD controller present / RST driver

problem: Valorant freezes on alt-tab or periodically (recovers after tabbing out) - Fullscreen Optimizations / MPO
symptoms: Game freezes randomly; alt-tab out and in restores it
Alt-tab sometimes freezes permanently
root_causes: Windows fullscreen optimizations / Multi-Plane Overlay conflicts

fixes.fix: Right-click VALORANT-Win64-Shipping.exe > Properties > Compatibility > Disable fullscreen optimizations; OP confirmed (another user it did not help)
Disable MPO using NVIDIA's registry script (works on AMD too); fixed months-long alt-tab freezes

problem: Valorant freezes/hangs because of conflicting software (RivaTuner) or missing admin rights
symptoms: Game freezes completely after clicking in menu (no music) or freezes 1-5 min in lobby with loading cursor

fixes.fix: Completely uninstall RivaTuner Statistics Server and reboot
Run Valorant as administrator

problem: Game crashes at launch/main menu fixed by reinstalling Vanguard
symptoms: Cannot start, or freezes at main menu; no logs or Windows messages

fixes.fix: Reinstall Vanguard (OP confirmed fixed)

problem: Crash after match starts / VAN -102 after driver updates (Intel drivers)
symptoms: Crash on match start, later VAN -102 on launch after Windows 10 driver update on Nitro 5 laptop (also after patch 13.01)
VAN-102/VAN-5 with 1 minute suspensions (no fix)

fixes.fix: Update all Intel drivers from Intel Driver & Support site; OP confirmed fixed
Contact Riot support for VAN-102/5 suspension issue

problem: Graphics drivers crashed - black screen, monitor reconnect (NVIDIA)
symptoms: Random freeze, black screen, monitor disconnect/reconnect, GPU usage spike to 100% for 1-2s, only in Valorant

fixes.fix: Riot-support steps: download latest NVIDIA driver, run DDU (Display Driver Uninstaller) 'Clean and restart', install driver, restart (OP says it solved after months; another user says it did not work for them)

problem: Corrupted game files crash during matches
symptoms: Crash when match starts or randomly in match with 'corrupted game files'; repair takes 40 min

fixes.fix: No fix found in thread (reinstall, repair, Windows reinstall did not help)

problem: Secure Boot cannot be enabled / Secure Boot Violation on enabling (VAN9003, VAN: RESTRICTION)
symptoms: Valorant requires Secure Boot but enabling it shows 'Secure Boot Violation' or black screen / boot failure
VAN:RESTRICTION lists TPM 2.0, VBS, HVCI, Secure Boot
root_causes: Secure Boot keys missing/invalid (PK/KEK/db) or BIOS OS type set to Other OS
Windows installed in legacy/MBR mode (EFI downloader issue)

fixes.fix: Enable fTPM (AMD) / PTT (Intel), Secure Boot, SVM/VT-x virtualization in BIOS, and Memory integrity in Windows; OP resolved after ~5 hours, also converting disk state
Install/enroll Windows default Secure Boot keys (reset keys to factory) before enabling Secure Boot; set OS Type to Windows UEFI mode
Update BIOS (ASUS EZ Flash with renamed CAP file on FAT32 USB)
Convert MBR to GPT if installed in legacy mode (OP found a way but unresolved)
Just turn Secure Boot on when it is simply off with no violation
Dual boot Linux: enable Secure Boot only to play, or use a distro with signed shim and enroll keys

diagnostic_signals: BIOS mode UEFI vs Legacy (msinfo32), disk partition style GPT/MBR

problem: Hardware-level 30-day Vanguard restriction (VAN: RESTRICTION 1)
symptoms: Secure boot verification failure message despite SB/TPM/virtualization/memory integrity on; Riot says 30 day hardware restriction
root_causes: Vanguard flags configuration prone to cheating (per Riot support)

fixes.fix: OP says they fixed it themselves (method not described)

problem: Incompatible OEM driver detected (MediaTek Wi-Fi mtkwl6ex.sys)
symptoms: 'Incompatible OEM Driver Detected' for MediaTek RZ616 Wi-Fi driver version 3.3, needs 3.5
root_causes: Outdated OEM Wi-Fi driver, possibly migrated from old PC via Microsoft account

fixes.fix: Factory reset Windows and set up as new PC (not restoring from old PC's account); MSI update tool then installed required Wi-Fi driver; OP confirmed
Install LAN/Wi-Fi driver from motherboard maker site and manually switch driver in Device Manager

problem: Low-end / laptop Valorant low FPS and stutter (Intel HD, MX230, thermal throttling)
symptoms: Fluctuating fps on Intel HD 4600/520, MX230, Ryzen 3500U, 8 GB RAM single channel
FPS drops to 60-90 on gaming laptops (CPU stuck at 1.8 GHz, thermal throttle)

fixes.fix: Guide (HP Probook i5-6200U, HD 520): latest Intel Graphics DCH driver, BIOS iGPU VRAM to 512MB, disable Turbo Boost (thermals), set all scalability groups to 0 in GameUserSettings.json, cooling pad
Debloat/optimize Windows 11 (one OP fixed 70-100 fps stutter)
Clean fans, repaste, laptop vendor performance profile, raise laptop for airflow
Lower resolution to 1280x720, close Medal and overlays
Set Memory Integrity off in Core Isolation; lock fps to 60
vgc.exe priority should be Normal
Add second RAM stick for dual channel

diagnostic_signals: CPU clock vs boost under load (throttling)

problem: Intel hybrid CPU stutter in gunfights - E-core scheduling / P-core saturation
symptoms: Stutter during fights on i5-13500/13600KF; visual desync / bullets appearing to pass through
root_causes: Windows schedules Valorant on E-cores or background apps saturate P-cores

fixes.fix: Task Manager > Details: set VALORANT-Win64-Shipping, VALORANT.exe, vgc.exe to High priority with affinity limited to P-cores; move other apps to E-cores; use ReservedCpuSets (valleyofdoom) to reserve P-cores then reboot

problem: Ping spikes on Ethernet - Vanguard/Riot Client efficiency mode
symptoms: Valorant-only ping spikes for months even on Ethernet
root_causes: Possibly Windows process throttling or onboard Wi-Fi module

fixes.fix: Manually set efficiency mode on Vanguard and Riot Client processes while Valorant runs (as reported by poster)
Disable integrated Wi-Fi module in Device Manager; close Riot Client after launch

diagnostic_signals: Process efficiency mode state of vgc/Riot Client

problem: Ping higher than before - local network hardware or Wi-Fi
symptoms: Home server ping 12-15 -> 40; network RTT+processing delay 30ms with Wi-Fi

fixes.fix: Switch the PSU power cable into a different wall socket; ping fixed (OP, unclear why)
Use Ethernet instead of Wi-Fi; run traceroute and bufferbloat test

problem: Wi-Fi throughput collapses while Valorant runs (Lenovo Vantage)
symptoms: Wi-Fi speed falls to 1-10 Mbps when Valorant launches, in-game ping fine; recovers when closed

fixes.fix: Install the newer Lenovo Vantage update; OP confirmed fix

problem: Voice chat muted for everyone / mic buzzing
symptoms: Mic and teammates muted, loopback works
Cannot hear teammates after new headphones
Mic buzzing in push-to-talk (Razer BlackShark V3)
root_causes: RGB controller software conflicting with Razer Synapse (buzzing)

fixes.fix: Toggle team/party voice chat off in lobby, play rounds, toggle on again; OP confirmed (not reliable for all)
Toggle team voice off then on once in Settings > Audio > Voice Chat, wait 10-20 s; or disable and re-enable network adapter
Remove conflicting RGB controller; OP reset PC

problem: No sound system-wide after launching Valorant with Sound Blaster card
symptoms: All sound (including Windows) disappears after game; only reboot fixes; TPM error on alt-F4
root_causes: Vanguard conflict with Sound Blaster AE-5 per support

fixes.fix: Use motherboard onboard audio while playing; problem later disappeared on its own for OP

problem: Stretched / true stretched resolution broken after patch 13.01
symptoms: Default 4:3/5:4 true stretched resolutions and GameUserSettings.ini method stop working
EasyTS tool no longer works
root_causes: Riot patch blocked 4:3/5:4 true stretch; ini method patched

fixes.fix: Create custom resolutions (e.g. 1568x1080, 1280x882) via CRU or GPU control panel; set Fill via game config then use Winexp/HRC (Hotkey Resolution Changer) to switch; repeated each game
Disable monitor in Device Manager, set windowed fullscreen native with Fill, switch resolution while in match/range
EasyTS tool (GitHub) edits GameUserSettings.ini - broken after the patch

problem: Doubled color saturation with stretched resolution
symptoms: Saturation doubles intermittently until alt-tab
root_causes: Resolution changed via Windows display settings

root_causes: Overlays/second monitor prevent independent flip; debloat removed Game Bar

problem: FPS locked at refresh rate after driver update
symptoms: fps locked to 180 on 180 Hz monitor

problem: Low FPS/stutter on high-end AMD builds (X3D, RX 9000) - general
symptoms: Low fps vs benchmarks on 7800X3D+9070XT; 500+ fps desync; random stutter

Cap fps to ~2x refresh not exceeding 500
Disable AMD ReLive/overlay, Radeon Boost/Chill; uninstall Ryzen Master; HDMI to GPU

problem: Misc: chat service unavailable, installer popup closing, version mismatch
symptoms: 'Chat Service Unavailable' empty friends after Riot ID change
Installer pop-up closes if clicked early
'previous version' mismatch
